desc:
A network has n servers numbered 0 to n - 1 and bidirectional cables, where edges[i] = [u, v] connects servers u and v. The network is not necessarily connected.

A server is a single point of failure (a cut vertex) if switching it off, together with all its cables, increases the number of connected groups of the remaining servers. Return all such servers in increasing order.

n = 6, edges = [[0,1],[1,2],[2,0],[1,3],[3,4],[3,5]]  -> [1,3]
n = 4, edges = [[0,1],[1,2],[2,3],[3,0]]              -> []    (a ring has no weak point)
n = 5, edges = [[0,1],[1,2]]                          -> [1]   (servers 3 and 4 are isolated)
constraints: 0 ≤ u, v < n and u ≠ v
No cable is listed twice (in either direction)
hints: The brute force removes every server and recounts the groups, which is O(n (n + m)). Look for a single pass.
Run a DFS and give every node a discovery time. For a node v, find the smallest discovery time that v's DFS subtree can reach with a single non-tree edge (its low-link).

A non-root node u is a cut vertex when some DFS child v has low[v] ≥ disc[u]: the subtree of v cannot get around u. The DFS root is a cut vertex exactly when it has two or more DFS children. Use an explicit stack because the DFS can be 5,000 levels deep.
editorial: Do a DFS over every component and record disc[u] (when u is first reached) and low[u] (the smallest discovery time reachable from u's subtree using tree edges downward and at most one back edge). Back edges connect a node to an ancestor, and the edge back to the direct parent is not counted.

Take a non-root node u and a DFS child v. All of v's subtree can reach something strictly above u exactly when low[v] < disc[u]. If instead low[v] ≥ disc[u], deleting u cuts v's subtree off from the rest of the component, so u is a cut vertex. Any one such child is enough.
The root has nothing above it, so it is a cut vertex precisely when it has at least two DFS children (those children's subtrees are unconnected once the root is removed).
The whole thing is one DFS, O(n + m). Isolated servers and leaves are never cut vertices.
